I'm 55, been farming this land for 30 years, and I have a university degree. That means I don't just do what my father did — I read the labels, I calculate rates, and I've been to enough extension trainings to know the science. But I'm also practical. My farm is only 4.1 mu, tiny by any standard, so I farm it intensively. Every jin of yield matters because my household has six mouths, and while some family members earn off-farm wages, the farm still puts food on the table and covers its own costs.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it last October, as always. Now it's early spring, and the wheat is waking up from winter dormancy. I will irrigate once at green-up to get it moving, then topdress with urea around jointing — about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total, split between base and topdress. I'll also put down compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium, roughly 6 kg P₂O₅ and 4 kg K₂O per mu. I have my own tube well, so water is secure but pumping isn't free; I'll irrigate three times total — green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I'll spray herbicide once in early spring, insecticide twice as the weather warms, and fungicide once at heading to protect against fusarium. I expect about 520 kg per mu if the spring doesn't turn dry. For tillage, I rotary-tilled before planting last autumn; there's nothing more to do now but manage the standing crop.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, the turnaround is brutal — maybe ten days. I will plant hybrid maize immediately, no-tillage direct seeding. I've learned over the years that wasting time on tillage between wheat and maize costs me yield more than it helps. The maize gets similar fertilizer — about 16 kg N, 5 kg P₂O₅, 4 kg K₂O per mu — banded at planting. I'll irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is too dry, and again at the big flare stage. Three pesticide applications total: pre-emergence herbicide, and two insecticide sprays for corn borer and armyworm. With good weather and timely water, I expect around 580 kg per mu from the maize.
